source_review.notes: Reviewed all ten references. General decomposition/partition/mapping design was checked against Foster's Argonne-hosted book; graph partitioning against primary Karypis-Kumar and Hendrickson-Leland records; current chunking/partitioner contracts against OpenMP 6.0, oneTBB, and Rayon; heterogeneous grain against NVIDIA guidance; communication/collectives against MPI 4.1; and graph-tool behavior against METIS. Nine sources resolved directly; the SIAM primary-paper DOI resolved but denied automated content retrieval, so its use is limited to durable bibliographic/algorithm attribution. A mismatched Cambridge DOI discovered during review was removed before this digest was signed.

The chapter separates scalar estimated useful cost, resource-cost vectors, actual elapsed time, communication, and ownership semantics.

evidence: Any P-resource schedule needs at least W/P by aggregate capacity and at least max c_i for an indivisible item; a fixed assignment needs at least max_j L_j.

evidence: Surface-to-volume, constant per-task overhead, cost estimates, and heterogeneous adaptive ratios are labeled models/heuristics rather than universal performance laws.
Executable limitations exclude dependencies, overhead, communication, migration, cache/NUMA/device effects, ownership transfer, faults, cancellation, optimality, and safety.

Cutoff/grain, task overhead, imbalance, locality, communication, NUMA, device ratios, memory high-water, cancellation, and recovery require the specified sweeps and environment metadata.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The sequential scalar model proves no optimality, real scheduling, speedup, migration correctness, fault tolerance, or deployment safety.

limitations: Internal authoring, source, mathematical, snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external scheduling, graph-partitioning, CPU/GPU, distributed, performance, power-grid, railway, regulatory, real-time, or functional-safety review is claimed.
